records.answer: Danske Bank's net profit for 2025 was DKK 23,037 million. That was a 3% decrease from 2024, when it stood at DKK 23,629 million. [1] The executive summary gives the same 2025 result rounded, as a net profit of DKK 23.0 billion [2].

cited_text: 2025 vs 2024 Total income increased 1% from the level in 2024, driven by strong net fee income, which benefitted from high performance fee income, higher investment fee income driven by growth in asset management and strong customer activity. Net interest income remained stable as the sale in late 2024 of the personal customer business in Norway and a decrease in deposit margins due to lower market rates were countered by an increase in lending. Operating expenses were largely unchanged, while impairment charges increased from a net reversal in 2024. Net profit decreased 3% and amounted to DKK 23,037 million in 2025 (2024: DKK 23,629 million), which was in line with the guidance published in the interim report for the first nine months of 2025.

The year 2025 was again a year of solid performance by Danske Bank as we continued to deliver on our Forward ’28 strategy to be a Nordic leader with strong profitability. The return on equity stood at 13.3% for 2025 based on a net profit of DKK 23.0 billion with a stable cost/income ratio and strong credit quality supported by stable and improving macroeconomic conditions. Customer activity was higher in several segments across our businesses, and we continued to grow in prioritised segments. Growth was primarily driven by corporate lending and strong traction in private banking activities and asset management, with record-high assets under management as we supported customers thanks to our well-capitalised balance sheet and expert advisory solutions.

Nordea treats AI as one of the forces its strategy depends on. The 2025 report says technology, data and artificial intelligence (AI) will play a critical role across the three priorities, supporting better customer experiences, growth and efficiency. [1]

AI already has practical uses at the bank. AI systems help predict customer churn, detect fraud and accelerate software development [2], and it also powers virtual assistants for customers and staff.

The next step is to widen AI's use into the core business. Nordea plans to extend it into its main product areas, with the aim of making processes smarter and more automated [2]. The report gives the example of a mortgage application, which should move from submission to approval in fewer steps, with processing time reduced significantly.

cited_text: Across our three priorities, technology, data and artifi­ cial intelligence (AI) will play a critical role – supporting better customer experiences, growth and efficiency.

Artificial intelligence (AI) will play an important role here. AI is used at Nordea in a variety of ways, for example to power virtual assistants that support customers and help colleagues in their daily work. AI systems also help predict customer churn, detect fraud and accelerate software development.

In the next phase, we will apply AI across our core product areas, such as mortgages, corporate lending, savings, and payments. In each area, we aim to make processes smarter and more automated, enabling large and complex tasks to be handled with greater efficiency. For customers, this means faster, smoother ­services. For example, a mortgage application should progress from submission to approval in fewer steps, with processing time reduced significantly.

In its 2025 annual report, Jyske Bank describes a cautious approach to AI. The bank takes a restrictive approach to the use and development of AI and new technology [1], and it aims for responsible implementation and measures that ensure transparency, robustness, and human control [1]. In practice, the bank's main AI uses reported for 2025 are these:

- Employee tools: In early 2025, Jyske Bank launched a new programme that supports Jyske Bank's AI journey. Overall, it revolves around equipping employees with new digital tools [2], with the aim of freeing time for more valuable work (that effectively free up time for more value-creating and motivating tasks to the benefit of employees, customers and investors alike [2]).
- Generative AI training: All employees in the organisation have been upgraded in the use of generative AI. All employees now have access to Microsoft Copilot [3], and they completed training in AI understanding, responsible use and practical application in M365 [3].
- Adviser support: the bank has new AI assistants and Co-pilot for advisers, helping to streamline processes [4], and these AI assistants support advisers in their daily work [5].
- Development approach: The development and deployment of AI solutions follow a risk-based approach that focuses on the responsible implementation of new technology [2].

Looking ahead, the report mentions AI in financial crime control. Towards 2028 further investments will be made in enhancing the quality and effectiveness of anti-money laundering (AML) and customer due diligence (KYC), by using AI and data integration, in order to ensure a compliant and robust IT set-up.
